brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume — you have four stronger alternates lined up.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for price in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range at higher volume or relaxed spec
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc; the verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec — so ask them to meet that lower band

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days after receipt — no reason to ease terms given the quality chaos

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny in absolute terms, which limits price leverage. But they're shipping us defective or mis-documented goods 40% of the time — that's a supplier who needs to earn our continued business, not dictate terms. The real leverage is walking: we have four credible rigid-packaging alternates (two listed, two large private converters) who can step in, so Scorpion cannot afford to lose us over a modest price move or a quality fix.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health score B 73/100) covering pails, containers, pharma — robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (marketBackups)
alternates.why: Manufacturer in India-East — a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ); maker rather than converter may offer tighter pricing

risks: The 40% return rate is a red flag for their process control or our spec clarity — if you push price hard before fixing quality, they may cut corners further and the rejection rate climbs.
Scorpion's financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on whether they're stable or one bad quarter from folding — keep the four alternates warm in parallel.
At ₹1.66 L annual spend, we're a rounding error to any serious converter — don't expect them to jump through hoops; frame the ask as 'meet market or we consolidate volume with a larger supplier.'

The market-backup leads (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Srichakra, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are unqualified research hits — verify capability and willingness to quote pharma-grade closures before citing them in the room.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We need to talk about the 40% return rate — that's costing both of us — and then align your price to the ₹0.65–0.80 band the market shows for this cap at volume.
